speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Differential geometry and Lie-algebra cohomology: announcement
summary: The dated heading announces work with Kazhdan on differential-geometric notions and Lie-algebra cohomology. No theorem or construction is written under it. The holomorphic-vector-field discussion above the date belongs to the preceding session.

speaker: B. V. Fedosov
title: Bibliography for vector-field residue formulas
summary: Fedosov supplies four references, including Bott\textquoteright s two 1967 papers and Baum--Bott\textquoteright s 1970 meromorphic-vector-field paper, and recalls the compact complex-manifold setting. Bernstein then develops the meromorphic version under his own heading.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Polar divisors and regularized Chern numbers
summary: The polar divisor of a meromorphic vector field produces a degree-two class \(\rho\). The notes replace the Chern classes by the coefficients of \(c(TX)/(1-\rho)\) before applying a zero-residue formula. Isolated zero and nondegeneracy assumptions are largely shorthand.

speaker: B. V. Fedosov
title: Pontryagin numbers from zeros of a Killing field
summary: A real analogue of Bott\textquoteright s formula uses a Killing vector field and the Pfaffian of its skew linearization. Compactness, nondegenerate isolated zeros, orientation, and characteristic-form normalization must be supplied.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Versal deformations of matrices
summary: Matrices depending on parameters are studied up to parameter-dependent conjugation. Jordan blocks explain singularities in the quotient, while transverse parameter families give versal deformations. Gelfand proposes a broader local picture for group actions and tensors, but the concluding conjectural language does not specify a mathematical category or equivalence.

speaker: A. M. Gabrielov
title: Griffiths on periods: bibliographical heading
summary: The entire entry is a heading and a reference to Griffiths\textquoteright s Annals papers, volume 90, number 3. The substantive exposition resumes in records 220 and 222; it is not retrospectively placed under this heading.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Quasihomogeneous singularities and a torsion preprint
summary: Bernstein reports Milnor--Orlik\textquoteright s formulas for the Milnor number and the monodromy divisor of an isolated quasihomogeneous hypersurface singularity. A brief comment connects polynomial-power distributions with cycles, and the page closes with news of the Ray--Singer preprint on analytic and combinatorial torsion.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Block determinants and positivity
summary: Gelfand recalls the Schur-complement factorization and a positivity criterion. The same subject occurred in item 1964-17.2. The notebook conflates nonnegative and positive-definite inequalities, so both precise versions are separated in the commentary.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Determinants of complexes and lens-space torsion
summary: An acyclic based finite complex has an alternating determinant, independent of the auxiliary boundary splittings. Twisted cellular complexes of lens spaces illustrate Reidemeister torsion. A nontrivial character is essential: the untwisted universal-cover complex is not acyclic.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Miniversal matrix families and centralizers
summary: The exposition of record 213 continues with a categorical description of induced deformations, an explicit nine-parameter family, and the centralizer-dimension formula. Transversality supplies versality; the notebook\textquoteright s description as a final object is stronger than the actual property.

speaker: L. D. Faddeev
title: Inverse scattering and Hamiltonian KdV
summary: The one-dimensional inverse-scattering solution of KdV is followed by its Hamiltonian structure and scattering action--angle variables, subsequently published by Zakharov and Faddeev. The final part concerns multidimensional scattering and a Volterra factorization of the scattering operator already announced by Faddeev in 1966. The notebook changes KdV normalizations without consistently changing all coefficients.

speaker: A. M. Gabrielov
title: Rational periods and tubes about a hypersurface
summary: Following Griffiths, rational differential forms are integrated over cycles avoiding their polar hypersurface. Projective compactification and a tube construction explain which cycles are relevant. Record 222 continues the homological and pole-reduction argument.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Real plane curves and the Gudkov congruence
summary: Harnack and Petrovskii bounds lead to Gudkov\textquoteright s modulo-eight conjecture for maximal curves. Arnold reports the modulo-four result and links it to characteristic elements of integral intersection forms on a branched double cover. The stronger congruence was proved by Rokhlin in a note received in December 1971.

speaker: A. M. Gabrielov
title: The tube exact sequence and Griffiths reduction
summary: The tube-map kernel is identified with the image of ambient projective homology. Homogeneous coordinates then give rational projective forms and a Jacobian-ideal formula reducing pole order. Two displayed formulas need explicit corrections: kernel means image of the intersection map, and the numerator degree depends on the pole order.

speaker: V. P. Palamodov
title: Characteristics of differential systems
summary: Palamodov argues that differential consequences must be included before assigning a characteristic variety to a system. The first example is corrupted as a mathematical formula even though the transcription follows the scan. The underdetermined divergence equation illustrates the difference between analytic existence and unique determination by Cauchy data.

speaker: S. Rolewicz
title: Linear orbits and the hypercyclic weighted shift
summary: Finite-dimensional orbit behavior is contrasted with the dense orbit of a multiple of the unilateral backward shift. The concatenation construction is sketched, with additional remarks on topological equivalence and algebraic operators unbounded in every norm.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Unimodular integral forms and characteristic vectors
summary: Arnold continues the arithmetic used for real curves: characteristic elements, the signature congruence modulo eight, and the classification of indefinite unimodular forms. Definite forms obey a finiteness theorem but are not classified merely by rank and signature. Serre\textquoteright s arithmetic text is recommended.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Sites, sheaves, and representations
summary: Kirillov presents material attributed to Geronimus: coverings in a category, the sheaf condition, and cohomology. For a finite group the site of finite group-sets recovers ordinary representations. Geronimus\textquoteright s short 1971 announcement and detailed article identify the Lie-group site and its comparisons with classifying-space and differentiable cohomology. The notebook confuses general morphisms with the submersions used in covering families.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: The elliptic-curve modularity conjecture
summary: The \emph{Weil conjecture} here is modularity of elliptic curves over \(\mathbb Q\), expressed by a modular parametrization, local Euler factors, and integrals of a weight-two modular form. It is not the Weil conjectures for varieties over finite fields. The handwritten cubic exponent is retained rather than silently normalized, and the treatment of conductors explicitly starts with \(p\ne2,3\).

speaker: A. M. Perelomov
title: Theta functions, coherent lattices, and uncertainty
summary: Integral symplectic lattices and quadratic refinements lead to theta-function identities and completeness of lattice coherent states. The critical-density deletion result was already published in Perelomov\textquoteright s February 1971 paper. A question about bounded centered position--momentum uncertainty for an orthogonal basis has a positive general answer; restrictions preserving a Gabor lattice change the answer. The final leaf P000360 is an adjacent out-of-scope record: Kirillov on 6 September 1971, not a continuation of this April session.
